No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 98, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders; His right hand and holy arm have gained Him the victory. 2The LORD has proclaimed His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations. 3He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. 4Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth; break forth—let your cry ring out, and sing praises! … 5 more verses PSALM 98 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 98
Let the whole earth his love proclaim With all her different tongues; And spread the honours of his Name In melody and songs. STANZA III
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 1. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.
